messages:
alex (AcmeCorp): hey team — our users can't finish OAuth sign-in with Google. they get bounced back to our app with an error page saying "state mismatch". happens intermittently (~30% of attempts). started after we deployed the frontend on the new domain.

maria (Support): thanks for reporting — can you paste the exact error you see and the full callback URL (redacted tokens ok)? also which browser and device?

alex (AcmeCorp): error page shows: "OAuth error: state_mismatch". callback looks like: https://app.acme.example.com/auth/callback?code=4/0AY0e-g...&state=Zk1lR2x...

Browser: Chrome desktop (most reports), also some Safari. deployment: nginx reverse-proxy -> frontend served from app.acme.example.com, backend at api.acme.example.com. Prior domain was app.acme-old.example.com — we changed CNAME and updated GCP OAuth client settings to new redirect URI.

maria (Support): ok. intermittent suggests race or cookie/same-site issue or a PKCE/state store mismatch. tagging eng: @olivia @raj — can you weigh in?

olivia (Eng): thanks. common culprits: 1) frontend stores the state/code_verifier in a cookie/localStorage and domain mismatch breaks retrieval; 2) double-URL-encoding of redirect_uri or state during roundtrip; 3) load balancer/proxy stripping or modifying query params.

Quick checks for Alex:
- In Chrome DevTools network tab, follow the redirect from accounts.google.com to /auth/callback. Confirm the state param on the request matches the state that your frontend generated (check localStorage or cookie).
- Check backend logs for attempted code exchange failures (invalid_grant or mismatch).

If you can paste a sanitized copy of the request and the stored state, we can compare.

alex (AcmeCorp): i grabbed a failing trace: request to /auth/callback had state=Zk1lR2x-abc123, but localStorage in the SPA shows state=Zk1lR2x-abc123 (matches) — weird. backend log shows: "state validation failed: expected Zk1lR2x-abc123 but got Zk1lR2x-abc123". literally the same string.

maria (Support): odd — same string but still failing. can you confirm whether the backend reads state from a cookie or receives it from the frontend? sometimes apps send state both in cookie and in form, and validation compares wrong sources.

alex (AcmeCorp): backend expects state in body POST during the code-exchange; frontend is sending it in query param and not including it in the POST. previous deploy included a small SPA change that moved the exchange code into a serverless function; maybe it forgot to forward state.

olivia (Eng): that could do it. For PKCE flows the backend often needs code_verifier and state during the server-side exchange. If the serverless function is invoked after redirect, ensure it reads the state from req.query and passes it through. Example minimal exchange flow (node/express):

```js
// server callback handler
const { code, state } = req.query;
const code_verifier = req.cookies['pkce_verifier'];
// verify state if you stored it server-side
if (!state || state !== req.cookies['oauth_state']) {
  throw new Error('state mismatch');
}
const tokenResp = await fetch('https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
  body: new URLSearchParams({
    code,
    client_id: process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID,
    client_secret: process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET,
    redirect_uri: process.env.OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI,
    grant_type: 'authorization_code',
    code_verifier
  })
});
```

raj (SRE): also check cookie attributes: if the PKCE verifier or oauth_state were set in a cookie on the old domain, SameSite or domain attribute might prevent the cookie from being sent to the new subdomain. For cross-subdomain cookies you need Domain=.example.com and SameSite=None; Secure. Browsers tightened defaults recently.

alex (AcmeCorp): we actually set oauth_state in localStorage (client-side) and the serverless function expects a cookie. we migrated some code and forgot to update the exchange. that explains the intermittent behavior — some requests hit an older instance that still reads localStorage via SSR and patches state.

maria (Support): nice find. two parallel fixes: update the serverless exchange to accept state from query if cookie missing (defensive) and patch the SPA to POST state/code_verifier to the exchange endpoint.

olivia (Eng): another quick check: ensure your OAuth redirect registered in Google Console exactly matches what's returned (including trailing slash). Example failure patterns we've seen: redirect_uri registered as https://app.acme.example.com/auth/callback but the app redirects to https://app.acme.example.com/auth/callback/ (extra slash) — Google will reject token exchange or you can get confusing failures.

alex (AcmeCorp): confirmed: registered URI had no trailing slash; for a period our deployed host appended a slash via nginx rewrite. i changed nginx to stop adding the trailing slash to that path.

raj (SRE): great. also check that the code_verifier storage survives navigation. If you store it in session cookie ensure path and domain are set correctly. If using SameSite=Lax, some POST redirects may not include it. PKCE verifier often needs to be persistent for the short redirect window.

alex (AcmeCorp): implemented two changes: 1) update serverless function to read state from query fallback and to log mismatches with full context (sanitized), 2) change SPA to send code_verifier to the server via a POST immediately after redirect handling. rolled to staging.

(After deploy)

alex (AcmeCorp): update — staging looks good, i forced 100 sign-ins and no state errors. rolling to prod in 10 mins. will report back if anything pops. :party_parrot:

maria (Support): awesome — glad it looks fixed. when you roll to prod, keep an eye on these logs:
- backend: oauth.state_validation.failures (count)
- oauth.exchange.invalid_grant (count + error message)
- browser errors showing missing cookies (console warnings about SameSite)

alex (AcmeCorp): rolling now. thanks everyone.

(resolved)

alex (AcmeCorp): confirmed in prod: problem resolved. one follow-up question: should we prefer cookies or localStorage for storing PKCE state? any security guidance?

olivia (Eng): prefer ephemeral cookies with Secure + HttpOnly when possible for server-read values. For SPA-managed state, localStorage is acceptable but be careful with XSS. If the server needs to validate state server-side, cookies scoped to the auth domain are simplest. Documented recommendations:
- code_verifier: store in a cookie with Secure attribute, SameSite=None if cross-site, short TTL
- state: can be double-checked both client and server, but avoid relying solely on localStorage if server validation is required

maria (Support): adding a short knowledge base snippet to our KB on common OAuth pitfalls (callback mismatch, PKCE verifier not forwarded, SameSite cookie issues). i'll attach the logs you provided (sanitized).

oauth-bot: note: ticket #S-4721 marked RESOLVED by alex (AcmeCorp).

alex (AcmeCorp): thanks all, appreciate the quick help.
